wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Space history and not Space reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

registry_rules: Standard cx.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a Move effect or legacy Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Anchor frontier, Move state_root, or reducer state.
Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into a shared Space Move/Anchor history.

Reducer-input durable kinds MAY declare cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, and bottom. cell_family is a stable cx.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, a payload field path, or a composite descriptor; lattice is one of or-set, mv-register, cas-register, fsm, counter, ordered-log; bottom is reject or expose.

State convergence is defined by Move preconditions/effects, Anchor DAG finality, and per-cell Lattice join. Compatibility Event Envelope fields are payload routing only and MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard cx.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form cx:<kind>:<id> unless a special form below applies.
Storage implementations MAY store raw IDs without the cx:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.
The raw ULID segment MUST use lowercase Crockford Base32 and MUST NOT contain i, l, o, or u.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Contrix core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.
Account, admin, applet, MIMI, media, moderation, directory, push, and key-management surfaces are optional or deployment-specific unless required by an advertised conformance profile.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces commonly needed by Events API, Principal Server, and clients.
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.
